title: Direct vs indirect free kick: the referee's arm tells you

scenes.text: If the referee raises an arm, that free kick cannot go straight in.
Difference one: scoring. A direct free kick can go straight into the net. An indirect one needs another player to touch the ball.
And if an indirect kick flies in untouched, it is not a goal. It is a goal kick.
Difference two: the offence. Direct: contact, like trips, pushes or holding, plus handball. Indirect: dangerous play, offside or the back-pass to the keeper.
Difference three: the box. A direct free kick offence inside the area is a penalty. An indirect one stays an indirect free kick.
So watch the referee's arm. Arm up: indirect.
Save it, and share it with whoever shoots at goal from every free kick.
